title: Austin Energy deploys 13 Pano AI wildfire cameras across its 437-square-mile territory
summary: The City of Austin's utility announced full deployment of a 13-camera Pano AI detection system covering its service area with the Austin Fire Department (29 August 2024); no detections are reported.
account: Austin Energy, the City of Austin's electric utility, announced the full deployment of a Pano AI system on 29 August 2024. It combines 13 ultra-high-definition 360-degree cameras, artificial intelligence and real-time monitoring across its 437-square-mile service territory. It covers most of Travis County and parts of Hays, Bastrop, Williamson and Burnet counties. Once a fire is identified the system alerts Austin Energy and local fire departments with location data and imagery. The utility says it supports decisions such as power shut-offs. Wildfire program manager Chris Vetromile and Austin Fire Department wildfire mitigation officer Justice Jones are quoted. Pano AI's Arvind Satyam is also quoted. The release reports no detection or contained fire. The source is the deployer's own announcement (a public body), with the vendor quoted inside it. No independent report is among the sources.
purpose: The cameras are deployed to detect and verify wildfires early and alert the utility and fire departments. The launch is the intended use with no outcome yet reported.
system: Pano AI wildfire detection system (13 camera stations)
deployer: Austin Energy (City of Austin) with the Austin Fire Department
taxonomy_note: No detection is attributable; the type names the loss-averting purpose of the cameras.

ratings.reason: No detection, response or saving is documented; the release describes capability only.
No outcome for the public is documented.

ai_role.statement: No event involving the AI is reported. The record documents the deployment only, from the public utility's own release that also carries the vendor's statement.
